sections.h2: Which office handles property tax in Caswell County?
sections.html:
The Caswell County Tax Office handles listings, exemption forms and bill payment, and it works from the courthouse at 139 E. Church Street in Yanceyville. Mail goes to PO Box 204, Yanceyville, NC 27379, the phone line is (336) 694-4194 ext. 5116, and the county directory lists weekday hours of eight to five.

The same directory entry explains how to pay a bill by card through an outside payment service. A fee applies, and it rises as the tax amount rises. Bill numbers begin with R for real estate or P for personal property, and you leave off the zero that follows the letter when you type the number in. The county home page also carries a Pay A Tax Bill link to an online bill search.

Two other offices matter to a seller. The Register of Deeds sits downstairs in the same courthouse complex and answers at (336) 694-4197. The county GIS office, on (336) 694-4194 ext. 115, matches parcels to maps. With a bill still open, call the tax office first for a payoff on the parcel.

sections.h2: What are the Caswell County property tax rate and revaluation dates?
sections.html:
Caswell County set its rate at 62.7 cents per $100 of value for property listed as of January 1, 2025, and the county was last reappraised effective January 1, 2024. The state schedule shows the next countywide reappraisal for 2028. The table gathers the figures exactly as the official documents print them.

The ordinance names ten fire districts: Anderson, Casville, Cherry Grove, Leasburg, Milton, Pelham, Prospect Hill, Providence, Semora and Yanceyville. Which one covers your house depends on the parcel, so ask the tax office when you want the exact combined charge for an address. For its rate-setting estimate the ordinance used $2,161,354,092 of real, personal and public service property and a 99.04 percent collection rate.

For the current year's rate, call the tax office or open the adopted budget ordinance on the county home page.

sections.h2: How does a Caswell County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
Value disputes go to the county's board of equalization and review, so begin by asking the tax office for the board's meeting dates and appeal form ahead of the spring session. The outline of the calendar comes from state law and is the same here as elsewhere:

  • The board's opening session lands somewhere from the first April Monday to the first May Monday.
  • Outside a reappraisal year the board wraps up about three Mondays after opening and generally stops by July 1. In a reappraisal year it has until December 1.
  • Request a hearing before adjournment, either in writing or by showing up. A decision notice mailed late in the session extends your window by 15 days from the mailing.
  • Its written decision is mailed within 30 days after it adjourns.
  • Still unhappy? Put a written notice of appeal to the Property Tax Commission in the mail within 30 days of the board's decision date, copying the county assessor.

The 2024 reappraisal is the latest, which ties the next large wave of appeals to 2028. In between, a value usually moves only after a physical change to the property, a clerical error or a change in permitted use, so a quiet-year appeal should name one of those.

The state's January 1, 2025 sales ratio study printed a median ratio of 104.97 for Caswell County. If your value looks high, gather recent nearby sales of comparable houses and dated photos of defects present on January 1.

sections.h2: Which property tax breaks can a Caswell County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
Three state homestead programs exist, and an owner can draw on just one. Applications use Form AV-9 and go to the county tax office. The county has to accept them up to June 1 before the tax year.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shelters half of a home's appraised value or $25,000, whichever is larger, for an owner who is 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled and whose prior-year income fits under the cap. The 2026 cap printed by NCDOR is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: waives $45,000 of appraised value whatever the applicant's age or income. Form NCDVA-9 is filled out with a Veterans Service Officer first.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: caps the bill at 4 percent of income for owners under the cap and 5 percent for those up to 150 percent of it ($58,200 for 2026), and the owner reapplies every year.

Sellers should know the circuit breaker's catch: the deferred amount is a lien, and a transfer makes the previous three fiscal years' deferrals payable. A house that used the deferment therefore carries an extra payoff on the closing statement.

The Caswell tax office page links the state's exemption, exclusion and present-use value forms, as well as business personal property listing forms.

sections.h2: How is the Caswell County tax bill handled at a sale?
sections.html:
The tax stays with the land, so an open balance is paid out of the sale at closing. The statutory lien for a given year takes hold on January 1, the listing date, along with later penalties, interest and costs.

A bill is due September 1 and costs face value until January 6. Interest then begins at 2 percent for the balance of January, followed by three-fourths of a percent for each month or part of one. A seller whose prior-year bill is open takes those charges to the closing table.

The deed adds its own charges. The transferor pays the state's conveyance excise tax, $1.00 per $500 of price or fraction, to the register of deeds ahead of recording, and statute fixes the recording fees ($26 for an ordinary instrument's first 15 pages, $64 for a deed of trust's first 35).

If a bill stays unpaid for long, the county may sue to foreclose the tax lien the way a lender would foreclose a mortgage, and the parcel goes to auction at the courthouse door. Redemption stays open until confirmation, on payment of what is owed.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Caswell County itself?
sections.html:
Caswell County is thinly settled, with 53.5 people per square mile in 2020. Yanceyville is where the courthouse sits, and Milton is the other town named on the county website. The Census Bureau counts 22,563 residents in its July 1, 2025 estimate, down 0.8 percent from the 2020 base, across about 425 square miles of land.

Homes are inexpensive here: the Census lists a $164,500 median for owned homes in 2020-2024, with owners living in 75.2 percent of them. Median household income comes to $59,755, and a quarter of residents (25.4 percent) are 65 or older, an age group the elderly exclusion is built for.

Workers average a 30.6-minute trip to their jobs. The county markets two industrial sites, the Pelham Business Park and the Yanceyville Business Park, and Piedmont Community College offers workforce training. County Environmental Health handles private septic permits, so a seller with a septic system can ask that office for the records on file.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Caswell County tax office?
faqs.a: Phone the tax office on (336) 694-4194 ext. 5116. The county directory puts it at 139 E. Church Street in Yanceyville, open Monday through Friday, eight to five. Keep your bill number handy and drop the zero after the R or P.

faqs.q: What is the Caswell County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2025-26 budget ordinance levied 62.7 cents on each $100 of property listed as of January 1, 2025. The same ordinance added 3.3 cents of fire district tax in the Casville and County Fire Service districts and set solid waste fees of $55 and $75. For the current year, ask the tax office.

faqs.q: When is the next Caswell County revaluation?
faqs.a: The state schedule shows 2028, following the reappraisal effective January 1, 2024. Counties must reappraise at least every eighth year and may choose shorter cycles. Confirm the date with the tax office, since schedules can move.

faqs.q: When are Caswell County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1 is the due date. Paying before January 6 of the next year costs face value, and from that day interest starts at 2 percent, moving to three-fourths of a percent monthly. A mailed payment counts on its postmark date.

faqs.q: Is a sale possible with Caswell County tax still owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Whatever is open, interest included, comes out of your proceeds at the closing table. Request a payoff figure from the tax office before choosing a closing date, and ask if a circuit breaker deferral adds a second balance.
